title: Paradise
question: What could be greater than a garden with rivers of milk and honey?
intro: The Quran describes Paradise, al-Jannah, in the language of gardens: shade, flowing rivers, fruit hanging low, no burning sun and no bitter cold. To people who first heard it in a dry land, these were the clearest pictures of a home without want.

Yet it also says the reality is beyond description: "no soul knows what has been hidden for them" (32:17). And its greatest gifts are not physical at all: hearts cleared of resentment, a greeting of peace, Allah's approval, and the sight of their Lord. Today you will see the four rivers, the ranks and gates, and what is promised beyond the gardens.

passages.context: Madinan, from Surah Muhammad. The verse ends by contrasting the drink of the Fire.
passages.point: Four rivers, each a perfected form of something known: water never stale, milk unchanging, wine that delights, honey made pure. And with them, forgiveness.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Makkan, from al-Hijr, right after the warning of Hell's seven gates (15:43-44).
passages.point: Paradise begins in the heart: every resentment is removed, and people sit as brothers facing each other, never tired, never sent away.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Madinan, from at-Tawbah. It names believing men and believing women together.
passages.point: Gardens, rivers and fine homes are promised, then the verse lifts higher: "approval from Allah is greater." That is the great attainment.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Makkan, from al-Qiyamah. A hadith in Muslim explains the "extra" of 10:26 as this sight.
passages.point: Radiant faces, looking at their Lord.
passages.label: differ
passages.note: Most scholars, with hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim, take this as a real seeing of Allah. The Mu'tazilah, an early theological school, read "looking at" as looking to, awaiting their Lord's reward.

visual.title: The four rivers
visual.caption: 47:15 names four rivers in Paradise, each a perfected form of a drink known here. A hadith in al-Bukhari adds that the rivers of Paradise spring from al-Firdaws, its highest part.

items.label: Wine
items.text: A delight to drink, with no headache or intoxication

word.nuance: From j-n-n, to cover or hide. A jannah is a garden so thick with trees that the ground is hidden. The same root gives jinn, beings hidden from sight, and janīn, a child hidden in the womb. Paradise is a garden whose fullness is still hidden from us (32:17).

mixup.myth: Paradise in Islam is only about physical pleasures, and mainly for men.
mixup.truth: The Quran promises Paradise to "believing men and believing women" alike (9:72, 33:35). Its pleasures are real, but it calls Allah's approval greater, removes resentment from hearts (15:47), and speaks of a joy no soul can picture (32:17). The highest gift, most scholars hold, is seeing Allah (75:23).

remember: The four rivers of 47:15: water, milk, wine without harm, and pure honey.
Hearts are cleared of resentment, and the greeting there is "Peace" (15:47, 10:10).
Allah's approval is greater than the gardens, and the faces of its people look at their Lord (9:72, 75:23).

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four rivers in 47:15?
quiz.why: 47:15 names rivers of water, milk, wine and purified honey. Oil is not among them.

quiz.q: What does 9:72 call greater than the gardens and dwellings?
quiz.why: 9:72: "...pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence; but approval from Allah is greater. It is that which is the great attainment."

quiz.q: What do the keepers of Paradise say at its open gates in 39:73?
options: "Peace be upon you; you have become pure"
quiz.why: 39:73: its keepers say, "Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein."

reflect: If Paradise begins with hearts cleared of resentment (15:47), is there someone you could begin to forgive now?
